authority_basis.claim_scope: Projectile launch velocity is resolved into horizontal and vertical components in a declared inertial frame.

concepts.statement: After launch in the standard no-drag model, horizontal and vertical motion share one state but have different acceleration components.
concepts.why_required: The two component equations describe one projectile and must remain coordinated under one physical model.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Horizontal and vertical motion may be treated as unrelated problems or gravity may be applied horizontally.

model_conditions.condition: Air resistance is neglected in the standard projectile model.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The horizontal acceleration is then zero and gravity is the only acceleration retained.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Horizontal velocity need not remain constant and the trajectory no longer follows the simple component equations.

model_conditions.condition: Gravity is uniform and vertically downward over the motion region.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The vertical displacement equation assumes constant acceleration.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: A position-dependent gravitational model is required.

model_conditions.condition: The declared observation frame is inertial for the standard component equations.
model_conditions.physical_reason: No pseudo-acceleration terms are included in the standard model.

representations.semantic_geometry: A curved trajectory is annotated with declared axes, signed launch components and a downward gravity vector to show one state decomposed into independent component equations.
must_not_imply: gravity acts horizontally in the standard model
horizontal and vertical motions use different times for the same event
representations.verification_method: Check horizontal constant-velocity behaviour, vertical sign convention and dimensional consistency of both component equations.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Declare the observation frame, axes and sign convention.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Velocity signs and gravitational direction become ambiguous.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Resolve the launch velocity into signed horizontal and vertical components.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The subsequent scalar equations may use the wrong launch state.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Apply zero horizontal acceleration and uniform vertical gravity only after the frame and launch state are fixed.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Gravity can be incorrectly applied to both axes or inconsistent time origins may be introduced.

required_transformations.description: Translate the launch vector into signed component state variables in declared axes.
Bind each component to its correct acceleration model while retaining the shared projectile state.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Gravity cancels or changes the inherited horizontal launch component in the no-drag model.
misconceptions.why_plausible: The visible trajectory curves, which can be misread as gravity continuously reducing all velocity components.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: At equal time intervals the standard model gives equal horizontal displacements even while vertical velocity changes.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Show a persistent horizontal velocity component with a separate downward gravity arrow.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Gravity contributes vertical acceleration only; horizontal velocity remains constant in the standard model.
misconceptions.verification: Use ax=0 and check the x relation remains linear in time.

problem_families.name: Projectile component evolution
recognition_cues: launch velocity with angle or components
problem_families.first_technical_move: Declare the frame and resolve the launch velocity before applying component kinematics.

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Remove the gravity-vertical-only invariant from projectile components.
